en: The Śivāpadānadaṇḍaka Stotra (The Hymn of the Staff of Śiva’s Exploits)

O you who dwell upon the mountains and other peaks, the ornament of the summit of Kailāsa; O you whose range is the ultimate reality, crowned with the crescent moon; O you who have reduced the bodiless god of love to ashes with a side-glance reddened by anger—a smile, a weapon, and the pride of the lineage of Śiva—with smiling corners of your eyes; O you who have accepted divine ash as a cosmetic for your limbs; O you whose left side is embraced by Gaurī; O you who have sanctified the region of human bones through physical contact; O you whose matted locks are illuminated by the waves of the Gaṅgā; O you who cause the entire circle of the earth to serve as the chariot for Indra, who delights in your salutation; O you who are the multitude of ascetics who have taken refuge in servitude to you.

You who have made the orbs of the sun and moon into a wheel; you who have struck down the ancient elephant [Gajāsura]; you who have taken up Mount Sumeru as your bow; you who have humbled the pride and expansion of the lineage of the Asuras; you who hold the grace of the bowstring like the Lord of Serpents (Śeṣa); you whose majesty is proclaimed by the great sages through the lute; you who possess the mastery of the arrow of manly prowess; you who have established the Supreme Person (Viṣṇu) in his station; you for whom the wind-eaters (the gods) performed the attire and the lotus-seated one (Brahmā) served as charioteer; you who are perceived as transcending the universe; you who have become the horse [in the form of Hayagrīva] and are the collection of primordial speech; you who remove the wonder of the jasmine with your mass of splendor.

O you whose peaceful three cities were destroyed by a mere fragment of a gentle smile; O abode of the realization of the digits of *nāda* and *bindu*; O most auspicious one; O you who manifested Vīrabhadra from a drop of perspiration; O you who brought under your control the terrified protectors and shattered the ritual system of Dakṣa’s sacrifice; O you who, with a blow of your palm, loosened the sun-like cheek of Brahmā as he bore various skulls upon his crown; O you whose fierce valor was displayed and who paralyzed the staff-like arms of the Cakrin; O you who possess great joy worthy of Brahmā’s hymns; O you who are invincible to those of crooked nature; O you who cherish the daughter of the Mountain-King!

O you who struck down the head of the Asura Jalandhara; O you by whom the Antaka (Yama), fallen in anger, was dispatched; O you who destroyed Sambara and Andhaka; O you whose matted locks acquired a supreme whiteness from the crushing of the bodies of others; O you who assumed the incarnation of Śarabha to subdue Narasiṃha; O you who liberated those who sought refuge from fear; O you who split open the eyes of Bhaga; O you who caused the burning away of the phenomenal world (prapañca); O you who took away the face of Viriñca (Brahmā); O you who purified Mount Mandara by your movement; O you who are exceedingly beautiful with five weapons; O you who removed the face of Dakṣa; O you who performed the act of wandering for alms; O you who wore a garland of flowers from the forest of Meru as an ornament.

He who has shattered the pride of the Kulapālikā of the Dārukāvana forest; whose devoted mind follows his every movement; who has turned back the malevolent spells of the arrogant ascetics; whose path is illuminated by the tiger skin that is the subject of Vyāsa’s words; who has rendered desire obsolete through his refined conduct; who has taken up the elephant hide as his garment; whose addiction to sin has been quelled by his own meditation; whose personal emblem is worshipped by the gods beginning with Brahmā; who is peaceful and compliant with the minds of others; who has forgiven the offenses of the ascetics; who is terrifying due to the flickering flames of the funeral pyre; and who is adorned with the Hālāhala poison.

O Gatekeeper protected by Nandin! You whose jeweled serpent-earrings possess the luster of the sprouts of the dawn’s rays; you who have bound the circle of the Ten-necked One’s arms with the tips of your feet; you who are ever-engaged in the dance of blissful *tāṇḍava*; you whose lotus-feet are worshipped by Govinda; you who grant joy to the thousand gods bowed in humility; you who bestowed grace upon Mādhava through his penance for the desire of a son; you who satisfied the son of Bhṛgu (Paraśurāma) by granting him divine weapons; you who are beautiful with the form of Hari manifested on the left side [of Śiva]; you who are praised by the Vedas; and you who are guarded by Nandin.

O You who are the object of devotion for the immortals headed by Indra, the hundred-fold secret of the Buddhas; O You from whom the ocean of milk was bestowed upon Upamanyu while he performed austerities for the sake of drinking its milk; O You who agitate the wicked who cause oppression; O You whose feet are not seen even by Hari and Viriñca; O You whose nature is the ever-advancing Dharma and who are supported by the Bull; O You who are intent on washing away unrighteousness; O You whose sovereignty is mounted upon the horse of the Vedas, whose form consists of the five Brahmans; O You who are inaccessible even to the Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad; O You whose delightful nature is free from fickleness; O You whose majesty in the kingdom of Akhaḍira is not small.

O You whose true nature is proclaimed by the *Atharvaśikhā*, who are delighted by the praises of the noble man free from pride, who are made known through the hymns of the best of Atharvans; O You who are to be contemplated at the end of sound (*nādānta*), who remove the suffering of those who bow to You, and who are the essence of the meaning of the *praṇava*; O You who are the support of charming loveliness, whose form is pure consciousness; O You who bear the venomous serpent, the Lord of the city of Kāśī; O You who sport within the lotus of the heart, whose dwelling is the sky of consciousness; O You whose sidelong glances reach to Your ears, who have conquered the god of love with Your ears like those of a bull; O You who are the comet of destruction for the cities of the fierce Asuras; O You who possess a smile, who reside on the bridge of Rāma situated upon the ocean; O You whose playful pastime is the act of protection.

Dwelling on Dakṣiṇa-Kailāsa, with eyes rolling slightly red, whose abode is at the root of the Ekāmra tree; who serves the terrifying moon; who purifies the peak of Śrīśaila; whose clusters of speech are as sweet as grapes; whose pillar-like arms are adorned with beautiful rudrākṣa beads; whose beauty is fashioned from the splendor of the dark-throated one; who bestows compassion upon the sacrificer Nīlakaṇṭha; a protector dependent solely upon service; the author of the tantras of the Śaiva Āgamas; the stable foundation for the triad of creation, maintenance, and dissolution; constrained by the Veda within the womb; to be meditated upon through the Gāyatrī; who has taken up residence in a choice bower-cottage; and who is difficult even for great beings to attain.

O Śivācārya, who have taught even the faces of Hari and Viriñci; O you whose infinite pastimes are worshipped; O coolness of Being-Consciousness-Bliss—be victorious, be victorious! Seeing the Kaustubha gem and even the host of Apsarases, how many gods did not engage in mutual debate? What burdens are there in this world other than those of heaven? When the poison had been expelled, when the host of gods had fled, and when the world was motionless, we praise only that Lord who appeared at the forefront with the words, "Do not fear! (mā bhaiṣṭa).
Thus ends the prose hymn on the deeds of Śiva, composed by the illustrious Nīlakaṇṭha Makhīndra.
